measured_on: 2026-10-01/02, Windows 11, i9-14900HX, RTX 4070 Laptop, .venv (Python 3.11, torch 2.4.1+cu121, mujoco 3.2.3)
harness: bench_stacked.py (this file was produced by the two ladders it defines)
machine_state: A Dreamer 1M-step run was training concurrently on the same laptop for the whole session, so the GPU was shared. This inflates every arm roughly equally and is the reason the end-to-end device factor here (1.68x) is smaller than the 3.5x measured earlier on an idle machine.

config.note: order alternated between reps so contention hits each arm about equally

n8_learner_bound.reading: At 8 envs a SAC run is learner-bound: ~76% of A2's wall clock is gradient updates, so the env rewrite is invisible (0.93x, inside the 11% rep spread) and the parallel backend is a 28% LOSS because 8 worker processes have to start. Today's default at this size (sync + cuda) is the only arm that beats where we started, by 1.56x.

config.note: learning gate closed, so this ladder measures collection alone

steady_state_for_contrast.caveat: 7328 excludes the time to start the worker processes. Over 600k steps the same configuration delivers 2062 env-steps/s end to end, because ~200 s of the 290.9 s is 32 child processes importing torch and mujoco.

n32_collection_only.reading: This is where the environment work actually pays: 1.22x from the hot-path rewrite and 1.86x from the parallel backend, end to end, at 600k steps. Extrapolating the measured startup (~200 s) and steady rate (6694 env-steps/s with the full wrapper stack) to a 1M-step collection gives ~2.1x over the committed sync backend.

committed_baseline_of_the_real_40M_run.source: mtime deltas between checkpoints/walker_target_v1/sac_actor_<step>.pt (38 segments under 40 min, two pauses excluded)
committed_baseline_of_the_real_40M_run.matches: the D32 arm of this file measures 1109 env-steps/s for the same shape of run (original env, sync, n=32)

device_factor_under_contention.reading: Both numbers are real; they were taken on the same hardware with different load. Quote the device factor with the wall-clock window it came from.

not_a_speedup.actor_gate: The committed gate `global_step % policy_frequency < num_envs` is always true when policy_frequency(2) <= num_envs, so the actor updated on every vector step instead of every other one. Fixing it removes wasted gradient work; arm D vs arm E above shows the corrected trainer costs the same wall clock as the old one within noise.
not_a_speedup.dreamer_recording: train_dreamer.py used to record only obs[0]/actions[0] of each collected vector step, discarding 3 of every 4 transitions. Fixed: the same env-step budget now yields 4x the data. That is a budget-quality change, not a clock change.
